THE SERVICE LINE WAS BURIED 15 1/2 INCHES FROM THE TOP OF GROUND TO THE TOP OF THE SERVICE LINE.     AFTER FINAL INVESTIGATION, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT SEVERAL FURTHER STEPS IN LOCATING AND EXCAVATION COULD HAVE BEEN PERFORMED TO HELP MITIGATE THE RISK OF DAMAGE TO THE GAS SERVICE LINE:    1.  DURING THE LOCATING PROCESS INSTEAD OF INDUCING A SIGNAL TO LOCATE THE SERVICE, A DIRECT CONNECTION COULD HAVE BEEN PERFORMED         TO INDUCE A LOWER FREQUENCY, POSSIBLY REDUCING THE CHANCES OF INTERFERENCE BY THE OTHER UTILITIES IN THE AREA.    2.  THE SIGNAL COULD HAVE BEEN " BALANCED" TO VERIFY THERE WAS A SYMMETRICAL MAGNETIC FIELD FOR THE SERVICE LINE.    3.  THE CONTRACTOR COULD HAVE UTILIZED A NON-INVASIVE EXCAVATION METHOD TO DETERMINE THE PRECISE LOCATION OF THE GAS SERVICE LINE          BECAUSE MECHANIZED EQUIPMENT WAS BEING UTILIZED WITHIN THE TOLERANCE ZONE OF THE LOCATE MARKS.

15348.NARRATIVE: GREG WARNER (PROPERTY WORKER) STATED THE FIRE ALARM SOUNDED, AND KITCHEN PERSONNEL STATED THAT GAS TO THE KITCHEN EQUIPMENT HAD STOPPED. MR. WARNER THEN WENT TO LOOK AT THE GAS METER, AND DISCOVERED A FIRE IN THE IMMEDIATE VICINITY OF THE METER. HE IMMEDIATELY CALLED THE FIRE DEPARTMENT UPON DISCOVERY OF THE FIRE.  PGS CUSTOMER CONTACT CENTER WAS THEN NOTIFIED BY THE FIRE DEPARTMENT OF THE FIRE AT THE BUILDING AND METER, AND OF A GAS LEAK. UPON ARRIVAL, THE FIRE DEPARTMENT EXTINGUISHED MOST OF FLAMES AT THE BUILDING AND METER. A SMALL FIRE REMAINED AT THE BASE OF THE RISER TRANSITION DUE TO ESCAPING GAS.  THE SERVICE LINE THAT WAS SUPPLYING THE RISER WAS THEN EXCAVATED BY HAND, AND SQUEEZED OFF TO PREVENT ADDITIONAL GAS FROM ESCAPING AND FUELING THE REMAINING FIRE.     IT IS BELIEVED THAT MULCH UNDER AND AROUND THE METER SET CAUGHT FIRE DUE TO A PROPERTY EMPLOYEE DISPOSING AN UNEXTINGUISHED CIGARETTE INTO THE MULCH. AFTER THE MULCH IGNITED, THE FIRE THEN COMPROMISED THE BOTTOM OF THE GAS METER, WHICH BREACHED THE METER CASING, THEN ALLOWED GAS TO ESCAPE AND FUEL THE FIRE. EXCESSIVE HEAT GENERATED BY THE FIRE THEN COMPROMISED THE INTEGRITY OF THE RISER. THAT RESULTED IN A BREACH OF THE SYSTEM AT THE TRANSITION RISER, WHICH FUELED THE SMALLER FIRE THAT WAS DISCOVERED AFTER THE BUILDING AND METER FIRE WAS EXTINGUISHED.  THE SMALLER FIRE WAS EXTINGUISHED AFTER GAS FLOW WAS STOPPED TO THE TRANSITION RISER.

ON JUNE 7, 2023, AT APPROXIMATELY 02:00 HOURS, PGS WAS NOTIFIED THAT A THIRD-PARTY CONTRACTOR HAD STRUCK A GAS PIPELINE AT STATE ROAD 31 & STATE ROAD 80 IN FT MYERS, FLORIDA.  RESPONDING CREWS WERE DISPATCHED AND ARRIVED TO FIND A SOIL SAMPLING RIG WAS THE CAUSE OF THE DAMAGED PIPELINE AND ESCAPING GAS.  AN ASSESSMENT WAS MADE OF THE SCENE, INCLUDING THE ABILITY TO SAFELY MANAGE THE SITE.      AN EVALUATION OF OPTIONS FOR THE ONE-WAY-FED 8" STEEL PIPELINE, CONCLUDED THAT THE PIPELINE WOULD REMAIN IN SERVICE TO CONTINUALLY SUPPLY APPROXIMATELY 25,300 CUSTOMERS DOWNSTREAM, UNTIL A BYPASS COULD BE INSTALLED TO ISOLATE THE DAMAGED SECTION OF PIPELINE.  OVER THE FOLLOWING DAYS, CREWS WORKED TO INSTALL 750' OF 8" STEEL BYPASS AROUND THE DAMAGED SECTION OF PIPELINE.  THE BYPASS WAS ABLE TO ISOLATE THE DAMAGED SECTION OF PIPELINE ON JUNE 10, 2023, AT 13:25, AND COMPLETE STOPPAGE OF THE ESCAPING GAS.      A ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION WAS CONCLUDED AND FOUND TWO PRIMARY CONTRIBUTING FACTORS:    1. THE GAS PIPELINE IN THE LOCATION OF THIS INCIDENT WAS/IS CLASSIFIED AS A "HIGH PRIORITY SUBSURFACE INSTALLATION (HPSI)" BY PGS THROUGH THE POSITIVE RESPONSE CODE OF "2C".  PER FLORIDA STATUE CHAPTER 556 HPSI REQUIRES SPECIAL PROCEDURES WHEN DIGGING NEAR AN HPSI. WITH THIS CLASSIFICATION, BEFORE ANY DIGGING OR DEMOLITION, THE EXCAVATOR MUST NOTIFY THE MEMBER OPERATOR OF THE START DATE AND TIME OF THE EXCAVATION.     IN ACCORDANCE WITH F.S. 556, THIS HPSI WAS MARKED BY PGS, AND A RESPONSE COMMUNICATED BACK TO THE REQUESTING EXCAVATOR USING A 2C (MARKED WITH EXCEPTIONS: HIGH PROFILE SUBSURFACE INSTALLATION IN CONFLICT).  THE INSTRUCTIONS PROVIDED AND COMMUNICATED TO THE EXCAVATOR INDICATED, "EXCAVATOR MUST NOTIFY THE MEMBER OPERATOR OF THE EXCAVATION OR DEMOLITION START DATE AND TIME" WHICH THE EXCAVATOR FAILED TO DO.  IN ADDITION, PEOPLES GAS ALSO SENT AN E-MAIL TO THE EXCAVATOR NOTIFYING THE EXCAVATOR ABOUT THE HPSI AND REQUESTING THE START DATE AND TIME. THE FAILURE BY THE EXCAVATOR TO NOTIFY PGS OF THE TIMING OF THEIR EXCAVATION AND THE SPECIFIC LOCATION DID NOT ALLOW PGS TO GIVE ADDITIONAL LOCATION INFORMATION AND SPECIFICATIONS RELATED TO THE PIPELINE IDENTIFIED AS "IN CONFLICT". THE FAILURE ALSO PREVENTED THE POSSIBILITY OF A PEOPLES GAS LOCATOR BEING ON-SITE DURING THE EXCAVATION.    2. THE DEPTH OF THE PIPELINE AT THE DAMAGED LOCATION WAS OVER THIRTEEN FEET DEEP.  WHEN PGS' LOCATOR PERFORMED THE INITIAL LOCATE MARKING, THE LOCATE SIGNAL UNKNOWINGLY JUMPED OFF THE GAS PIPELINE ONTO AN ADJACENT TELECOMMUNICATION FACILITY.  THIS CAUSED THE LOCATE MARKINGS TO VEER OFF THE GAS PIPELINE BY APPROXIMATELY 36" TO 48" AT THE DAMAGED LOCATION.

15348.MAP_EIGHT_CAUSE: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD
15348.NARRATIVE: ON DECEMBER 18, 2023, AT APPROXIMATELY 09:02 HOURS, PGS WAS NOTIFIED BY THE PUBLIC OF A GAS ODOR AT 3264 LONGLEAF PINE PARKWAY, ST. JOHNS COUNTY FLORIDA. RESPONDING CREWS WERE DISPATCHED AND UPON ARRIVAL, CONFIRMED THERE WAS AN ACTIVE LEAK.  THE PIPELINE WAS EXCAVATED AND SQUEEZED OFF, STOPPING THE ESCAPING GAS TO MAKE SAFE AT 15:45. AN ASSESSMENT WAS MADE OF THE SCENE, INCLUDING THE ABILITY TO SAFELY MANAGE THE SITE. AN EVALUATION OF OPTIONS FOR THE ONE-WAY FEED PE PIPELINE CONCLUDED THAT IT WAS SAFER TO TAKE THE LINE OUT OF SERVICE TO SAFELY INSTALL A BYPASS. AS A RESULT, 1,534 CUSTOMERS WERE OUT OF SERVICE. THE REPAIR WAS COMPLETED, AND RESTORATION OF THE AFFECTED CUSTOMERS WAS COMPLETED.      PGS CREWS IDENTIFIED THE SOURCE OF THE LEAK AS A PLASTIC FUSION OF THE 6-INCH MAIN.  THE FUSION WAS CUT OUT AND SENT TO A TESTING AND ANALYSIS LAB TO IDENTIFY THE CAUSE.  THE TESTING FACILITY IDENTIFIED THE PLASTIC FUSION AS A FAILED WELD WITH TWO POTENTIAL CONTRIBUTORS, #1 - SURFACE CONTAMINATION OF THE FUSION INTERFACE PRIOR TO JOINING (E.G., DUST FROM SURROUNDING ENVIRONMENT) AND/OR #2 - REMOVAL OF THE JOINING FORCE SHORTLY AFTER THE BEAD WAS PUSHED OUT (E.G., INADVERTENT SWITCHING OF BUTT-FUSION MACHINE'S HYDRAULIC PRESSURE TOGGLE LEVER) PREMATURELY.       PGS HAS IMPLEMENTED THEIR PROCEDURE FOR A FUSION INVESTIGATION OF SEVERAL ADJACENT BUTT-FUSIONS TO CONFIRM PROPER PROCEDURES WERE FOLLOWED FOR A SAFE INSTALLATION OR DETERMINE IF ADDITIONAL FUSIONS NEED TO BE REPLACED.  THIS EXERCISE IS EXPECTED TO TAKE SEVERAL MONTHS FOR EXCAVATION, REMOVE/REPLACEMENT AND TESTING OF THE SAMPLE FUSIONS.

APPROXIMATELY 89 CUSTOMERS EXPERIENCED SERVICE DISRUPTIONS DUE TO THE DAMAGE. A NEW REGULATOR STATION WAS INSTALLED ON THE NIGHT OF THE INCIDENT, WITH ALL REPAIRS COMPLETED THE SAME NIGHT. RESTORATION OF THE PIPELINE BEGAN THE NEXT DAY AT 8:00 AM AND WERE COMPLETED ON TUESDAY, JANUARY 28, 2025.    THE IMPACT OF THE INCIDENT IS STILL BEING EVALUATED WITH ADDITIONAL INFORMATION SUPPLIED IN FUTURE REPORTING.

ON THURSDAY, DECEMBER 4, 2025, PEOPLES GAS SYSTEM, INC. (PGS) WAS NOTIFIED OF A RUPTURED GAS LINE IN EUSTIS. PGS DOES NOT KNOW THE PRECISE TIME OF THE RUPTURE. HOWEVER, THE EUSTIS FIRE DEPARTMENT RECEIVED THE REPORT AT 9:32 A.M. THE FIRE DEPARTMENT CALLED PGS AT 9:43 A.M. PGS ARRIVED ON SCENE AT 10:05 A.M. AND SQUEEZED OFF THE MAIN TO STOP GAS FLOW AT 10:48 A.M. THE EXPLOSION OCCURRED NINE MINUTES LATER, AT 10:57 A.M. ONE PERSON WAS INJURED AND TRANSPORTED TO AN AREA HOSPITAL. SHE LATER PASSED AWAY. THE INVESTIGATION SHOWED THAT THE PIPELINE WAS DAMAGED BY AN EXCAVATOR HORIZONTAL DIRECTIONAL DRILLING CONDUIT FOR ANOTHER UTILITY WITH NO CONNECTION TO PGS. THE DAMAGE OCCURRED UNDER CONCRETE ADJACENT TO THE BUILDING THAT EXPLODED. WHEN THE DAMAGE TO THE GAS MAIN OCCURRED, THE EXCAVATOR WAS DRILLING MORE-OR-LESS PARALLEL TO THE GAS MAIN AND WITHIN THE TOLERANCE ZONE. PEOPLES GAS ACCURATELY MARKED THE FACILITIES ON NOVEMBER 19, 2025, WHICH MARKS REMAINED IN PLACE ON DECEMBER 4. THE INVESTIGATION SHOWED THAT THE DAMAGED MAIN RESIDED AT A HORIZONTAL DISTANCE OF APPROXIMATELY 15-18 INCHES FROM THE “ZERO LINE” OF THE MARKS, WITHIN THE 24-INCH TOLERANCE ZONE. (WE PROVIDE A RANGE BECAUSE THE DRILL PUNCTURED 10 HOLES IN THE MAIN, WHICH HOLES SPANNED AN APPROXIMATE 4-FOOT DISTANCE ALONG THE PIPE. THE POINTS OF DAMAGE ON THE PIPE RANGED FROM APPROXIMATELY 15 TO 18 INCHES FROM THE “ZERO LINE” OF THE MARKS.) PEOPLES GAS’ RESPONDERS INVESTIGATED TO DETERMINE WHETHER THE EXCAVATOR POTHOLED TO EXPOSE THE GAS MAIN BUT FOUND NO EVIDENCE THAT THE EXCAVATOR DID SO.     THE INVESTIGATION IS ONGOING, BUT THE CAUSE OF THE INCIDENT APPEARS TO BE THE EXCAVATOR’S FAILING TO MAINTAIN APPROPRIATE CLEARANCE FROM THE MARKS, FAILING TO USE INCREASED CAUTION WHILE DRILLING WITHIN THE TOLERANCE ZONE, AND FAILING TO EXPOSE THE GAS MAIN BEFORE DRILLING IN THE TOLERANCE ZONE. BECAUSE CONCRETE COVERED THE SURFACE OF THE GROUND ABOVE AND AROUND THE POINT OF DAMAGE, THE GAS APPARENTLY MIGRATED INTO THE NEARBY BUILDING THAT EXPLODED. PGS CONTINUES TO INVESTIGATE THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE INCIDENT AND CORRECTIVE ACTION.    ADDITIONAL NOTES: (1) THE FIRE DEPARTMENT EVACUATED NEARBY BUILDINGS. PEOPLES GAS DOES NOT KNOW THE NUMBER OF BUILDINGS EVACUATED. BECAUSE OF THIS UNKNOWN, WE HAVE IDENTIFIED “1” IN RESPONSE TO QUESTION 22, ABOVE; (2) WITH RESPECT TO PART D QUESTION 2E, ABOVE, THE LAKE COUNTY PROPERTY APPRAISER VALUES THE BUILDING AT $148,299 BEFORE THE EXPLOSION. WE UNDERSTAND THAT THE BUILDING CONTAINED A BUSINESS WITH MERCHANDISE AND A RESIDENCE. PGS DOES NOT KNOW WHETHER THE BUILDING SUFFERED A CATASTROPHIC TOTAL LOSS, AND PGS HAS NO ESTIMATE FOR THE VALUE OF ITS CONTENTS. PGS CONTINUES TO COLLECT TIME SHEETS AND CONTRACTOR INVOICES TO DETERMINE THE VALUE OF THE DAMAGE TO GAS FACILITIES; (3) WITH RESPECT TO PART A QUESTION 21C, PEOPLES GAS CANNOT ESTIMATE THE VOLUME OF GAS CONSUMED IN THE EXPLOSION.

31191.NARRATIVE: THE 1" CTS, SDR 11.5, ALDYL-A PIPE AND 1" SOCKET FUSION COUPLING WERE DIRECTLY UNDER THE FOOTING AND FOUNDATION OF 4601 WILLOWDALE LANE.    THERE APPEARED TO BE EXTERNAL DAMAGE TO THE 1" COUPLING AND THE 1" CTS PIPING APPEARS TO HAVE BEEN LOWERED IN PLACE BY THE HOME BUILDER.    THE 1" CTS PIPING WAS A DEAD END SERVICE STUB AND WAS UNKNOWINGLY OPERATING AT 230 PSI DUE TO A PREVIOUS UPRATE OF A 10" STEEL PIPELINE.    THE 1" CTS, SDR 11.5, ALDYL-A PIPE AND 1" SOCKET FUSION COUPLING WERE SUBJECT TO A SHOCKWAVE CREATED BY THE HOME EXPLOSION.    THE 1" CTS, SDR 11.5, ALDYL-A PIPE AND 1" SOCKET FUSION COUPLING IS BEING SENT TO AN INDEPENDENT LAB FOR A FORENSIC INVESTIGATION AND TESTING.    4/12/2019:  LAB TESTING RESULTS WERE RECEIVED FROM TWO THIRD PARTY CONSULTANTS.  RESULTS INDICATED THAT THE 1" COUPLING FAILED DUE TO SLOW CRACK GROWTH PROPAGATION AS A RESULT OF MULTIPLE STRESSES BEING APPLIED TO THE FITTING.  PER THE REPORTS, THE CRACK GROWTH AND LEAK POINT ON THE COUPLING WAS CONSISTENT WITH A TENSILE LOAD ON THE COUPLING.  THE PHENOMENA OF A BRITTLE CRACK WHICH STARTS IN THE LOCATION WHERE THE HEAT FUSION JOINED TUBING TERMINATES ON THE INTERIOR OF A SOCKET FUSION HAS BEEN DOCUMENTED PREVIOUSLY IN INDUSTRY.  THE CRACK FORMED BY THE NOTCH GEOMETRY CREATED BY THE INSERTED TUBING AND ITS POINT OF HEAT FUSION JOINING TO THE SOCKET WHICH, WHEN UNDER GAS PRESSURE, CAN CREATE A STRESS RISER.  THE NOTCH GEOMETRY MAY HAVE BEEN CONTRIBUTED BY THE SOCKET FUSION TOOLS AVAILABLE AT THE TIME OF INSTALLATION.  THE FAILURE IS ALSO CONSISTENT WITH INDUSTRY KNOWLEDGE OF ALDYL-A PIPE AND FITTINGS MANUFACTURED PRIOR TO 1984 AND SUSCEPTIBILITY TO INNER WALL CRACKING.  THE COUPLING WAS 10" UNDER THE FOUNDATION OF THE GARAGE AND APPEARED TO BE LOWERED IN PLACE DURING THE CONSTRUCTION OF THE STRUCTURE.  LOWERING WOULD HAVE CAUSED TENSILE STRESS ON THE PIPE AND COUPLING.  NO EXTERNAL DAMAGES WERE SEEN ON THE PIPE OR COUPLING FROM CONSTRUCTION OF THE GARAGE STRUCTURE.  AGAIN PER THE REPORTS, THE INTERNAL PRESSURE IN THE PIPE MAY HAVE ACCELERATED THE FAILURE IN THE COUPLING BUT COULD NOT BE DETERMINED AS THE SOLE ROOT CAUSE OF THE FAILURE.  THE TIME TO FAILURE FROM CRACKING COULD NOT BE ESTIMATED OR DETERMINED IN EITHER REPORT.    11/19/2019 - SUBMITTED AS FINAL REPORT WITHOUT FURTHER CHANGES AT THIS TIME.

SPD SECURED THE SCENE AND WERE ONLY ALLOWING EMERGENCY PERSONNEL PAST A CHECKPOINT ~0.2 MILES FROM THE SCENE. SCUD GIS MAPS WERE REVIEWED TO ASSESS THE LOCATION OF THE GAS SERVICE LINE TO CABIN 4020, ALONG WITH THE GAS MAINS AND VALVES IMMEDIATELY UPSTREAM AND DOWNSTREAM OF THE METER. SCUD EMPLOYEES OPERATED COMBUSTIBLE GAS INDICATORS (CGI'S) TO MONITOR THE PRESENCE OF NATURAL GAS IN THE AIR AROUND THIS LOCATION.      THE SUPPLY OF NATURAL GAS IS A 2'PE MAIN WITH A ONE-WAY SUPPLY OPERATING AT 45 PSIG. SCUD VALVE #71L 17 (LOCATED ~250' UPSTREAM OF THE CABIN) WAS OPERATED AT ~9:45 PM TO TURN THE GAS OFF. THE DOWNSTREAM SCUD VALVE #71L 6 (LOCATED ~1,550' DOWNSTREAM OF THE CABIN) WAS ALSO OPERATED TO LIMIT THE LOSS OF GAS AND IN HOPES OF MAINTAINING PRESSURE FOR THE 88 CUSTOMERS DOWNSTREAM OF VALVE #71L 17. THE 3/4' PE GAS SERVICE LINE TO 604 WALNUT WAY WAS EXPOSED BY HAND-DIGGING AND THE LINE WAS SQUEEZED OFF. THIS SERVICE LINE WAS INSTALLED ON 2-19-1993, SO THERE WAS NO EXCESS FLOW VALVE. THE 'LINEPACK' VOLUME OF GAS STORED IN THE PIPELINE DOWNSTREAM OF VALVE #71L 6 WAS CONSUMED BY THE DOWNSTREAM CUSTOMERS AND THE MAIN LINE WENT FLAT BEFORE THE GAS SERVICE ON THE MAIN COULD BE RESTORED. AT 11:20 PM, THE FIRE DEPARTMENTS REPORTED THAT THE FIRE IS CONTAINED. GAS SERVICE WAS RESTORED ON THE 2'PE MAIN AT APPROXIMATELY 11:30 PM. THE TEMPERATURE WAS 35F AND CUSTOMERS NEEDED HEAT FOR THE NIGHT. ADDITIONAL SCUD PERSONNEL WAS CALLED IN TO ASSIST WITH THE RESTORATION OF SERVICE AND LIGHT-UPS OF THE GAS APPLIANCES. NATURAL GAS SERVICE WAS RESTORED TO ALL OF THE 88 AFFECTED HOMES (EXCEPT TWO UNOCCUPIED CABINS) WHEN SCUD EMPLOYEES LEFT THE SCENE EARLY SUNDAY MORNING.    JAMES GREENE CALLED TENNESSEE PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION'S (TPUC) GAS PIPELINE SAFETY DIVISION (GPSD) DEPUTY DIRECTOR TRAVIS ASLINGER TO NOTIFY HIM OF THE INCIDENT AT 10:47 PM ON SATURDAY, NOVEMBER 16. 22784.NARRATIVE: ON TUESDAY, APRIL 7, 2020, AT APPROXIMATELY 7:10 P.M., A WISCONSIN POWER AND LIGHT COMPANY (WPL) PRESSURE REGULATION STATION LOCATED ON PRAIRIE AVENUE IN BELOIT, WISCONSIN, WAS STRUCK AND DAMAGED BY A VEHICLE. PRAIRIE AVENUE IS A TWO-WAY NON-DIVIDED ROAD WITH A POSTED SPEED LIMIT OF 40 MPH. THE STATION IS LOCATED APPROXIMATELY 35 FEET EAST OF THE ROAD AND THE STRETCH OF ROAD IS STRAIGHT. A 2008 FORD F350 PICKUP TRUCK TRAVELING NORTH ON PRAIRIE AVENUE AT A HIGH RATE OF SPEED LOST CONTROL, HIT THE CURB, LEFT THE ROAD AND STRUCK THE STATION'S TRAFFIC BARRIER AND PRESSURE REGULATION STATION. THE TRUCK SUBSEQUENTLY OVERTURNED SEVERAL TIMES AND ENDED UP NORTH OF THE PRESSURE REGULATION STATION. AS A RESULT OF THE MOTOR VEHICLE ACCIDENT, THE DRIVER OF THE VEHICLE WAS FATALLY INJURED AND ANOTHER OCCUPANT WAS INJURED AND TRANSPORTED TO A LOCAL HOSPITAL. THE POLICE REPORT NOTES THAT THE DRIVER WAS EXCEEDING THE SPEED LIMIT AND THEIR SPEED WAS TOO FAST FOR CONDITIONS. THE DAMAGE FROM THE VEHICLE CAUSED LEAKS ON THE PRESSURE REGULATING STATION PIPING.    WPL'S CUSTOMER SERVICE CENTER (CSC) WAS NOTIFIED AT APPROXIMATELY 7:16 P.M. BY THE 911 DISPATCH CENTER OF THE INCIDENT. THE CSC EMPLOYEE NOTIFIED WPL'S DISTRIBUTION SYSTEM OPERATIONS (DSO) OF THE ACCIDENT AT 7:21 P.M.  WPL FIELD PERSONNEL WERE DISPATCHED TO THE SITE AT APPROXIMATELY 7:30 P.M. AND ARRIVED AT THE SITE AT APPROXIMATELY 7:44 P.M.  WPL FIELD PERSONNEL CLOSED THE STATION INLET VALVE AND THE STATION OUTLET VALVE AT APPROXIMATELY 8:00 P.M.  THIS SHUT OFF GAS FLOW TO THE STATION AND RESULTED IN THE LOSS OF GAS SERVICE TO 111 CUSTOMERS.    WPL FIELD PERSONNEL BEGAN SHUTTING RISER VALVES FOR THE CUSTOMERS THAT LOST SERVICE SHORTLY AFTER THE FLOW OF GAS TO THE STATION WAS STOPPED.  REPAIRS TO THE REGULATION STATION STARTED SHORTLY BEFORE MIDNIGHT AND WERE COMPLETED BY APPROXIMATELY 6:00 A.M. ON APRIL 8, 2020.  THE RESTORATION OF GAS SERVICE TO CUSTOMERS STARTED AT APPROXIMATELY 8:00 A.M. ON APRIL 8, 2020.    AT THE TIME OF THE INCIDENT, THE PRESSURE REGULATION FACILITY AT PRAIRIE AVENUE AND E. INMAN PARKWAY WAS OPERATING AT: 105 PSIG INLET PRESSURE (115 PSIG MAOP) AND 54 PSIG OUTLET PRESSURE (60 PSIG MAOP).    NOTE: THE FATALITY TO THE DRIVER AND HOSPITALIZATION OF THE PASSENGER WERE A RESULT OF INJURIES SUSTAINED DURING THE MOTOR VEHICLE ACCIDENT. THEY WERE NOT RELATED TO THE RELEASE OF NATURAL GAS FROM THE DAMAGED PRESSURE REGULATION STATION. INMAN PARKWAY AND APPROXIMATELY 35 FEET EAST OF PRAIRIE AVENUE ON EASEMENT.

32601.NARRATIVE: ON MARCH 1, 2021 A KENTUCKY FRONTIER GAS EMPLOYEE SAW A HOUSE FIRE INCIDENT ON A SOCIAL MEDIA POST AT 9:23 AM, AND RECOGNIZED IT AS A GAS CUSTOMER.  THERE IS A FRONTIER LOGO & PHONE NUMBER ON THE GAS METER AT THIS HOUSE. THE LOCAL FIRE DEPARTMENT RESPONDED TO THE INCIDENT AT 2AM, OR 7 HOURS EARLIER, BUT MADES NO CALL TO OUR EMERGENCY LINE. FRONTIER IMMEDIATELY CALLED PIKE COUNTY EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT AND GOT INFORMATION AS TO THE TIME OF THE INCIDENT, THE RESPONDING FIRE DEPARTMENT AND DETAILS REPORTED BY A NEIGHBOR. THE 911 CALLER HAD REPORTED A HOUSE ON FIRE AND STATED HE HAD WITNESSED AN EXPLOSION.   A FRONTIER UTILITY FIELD TECHNICIAN ARRIVED AT THE RESIDENCE AT 10:36 AM AND SHUT OFF THE GAS FLOW TO THE HOME. A LEAK SURVEY TECHNICIAN ARRIVED AT 1:39 PM AND TESTED THE SOIL FOR POSSIBLE GAS LEAKS ALONG THE UTILITY SERVICE LINE.  BAR HOLE TESTS WERE MADE WITH A GAS MEASUREMENT INDICATOR AND A RMLD. GAS WAS DETECTED AT POINTS ALONG THE OPERATOR'S SERVICE LINE TO THE METER, AS WELL AS SOME MIGRATION TOWARD THE HOME IN LOW PPM CONCENTRATION. MORE DETAILED TESTING WAS DONE THE NEXT DAY MARCH 2.  THE SERVICE LINE WAS DEACTIVATED AND CAPPED OFF AT THE MAIN LINE.  ON APRIL 13 AT THE DIRECTION OF KENTUCKY PSC, FRONTIER EXCAVATED AND UNCOVERED A PORTION OF THE STEEL GAS SERVICE LINE FROM THE MAIN TO THE METER RISER.  FRONTIER TECHNICIANS DISCOVERED CORROSION PITTING AND A 1/16" PIT THROUGH THE PIPE WALL APRX 21 FT. UPSTREAM OF THE METER. THIS CORROSION PIT WAS DETERMINED TO BE THE SOURCE OF THE GAS DETECTED BY THE BAR HOLE TESTING.    THE CUSTOMER SERVICE LINE APRX 20 FT LONG FROM THE FRONTIER METER TO THE HOME WAS PRESSURE TESTED BY A SEPARATE PARTY.  TEST RESULTS DID NOT INDICATE A LEAK.   THE STATE FIRE MARSHAL REPORT WAS ISSUED JUNE 24.  THE MARSHAL CONCLUDES THAT THE FIRST FUEL IGNITED WAS NATURAL GAS, PRESENT IN THE GROUND FLOOR BELOW THE LIVING SPACE. THE PRECISE SOURCE OF THE IGNITED GAS IS UNDETERMINED.  THE UTILITY FOUND A LEAK IN THE SERVICE LINE ABOUT 40 FT AWAY, OUTSIDE THE FOUNDATION; AND THE FIRE INVESTIGATOR FOUND A CRACKED GAS LINE TO A UNIT HEATER LESS THAN 10 FT AWAY, IN THE GROUND FLOOR MECHANICAL ROOM UNDER THE HOUSE.  THE SOURCE OF IGNITION WAS UNDETERMINED.        A KENTUCKY FRONTIER GAS EMPLOYEE SAW THIS INCIDENT ON A SOCIAL MEDIA POST AT APPROXIMATELY 9:23 AM ON THE DATE OF 3/1/2021.  ALTHOUGH THERE IS A COMPANY LOGO & PHONE NUMBER ON THE GAS METER, THERE WAS NO CALL MADE TO OUR EMERGENCY LINE BY THE FIRE DEPARTMENT WHO RESPONDED TO THE INCIDENT 7 HOURS EARLIER. UTILITY IMMEDIATELY CALLED PIKE COUNTY EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT AND GOT INFORMATION AS TO THE TIME OF THE INCIDENT, THE RESPONDING FIRE DEPARTMENT AND DETAILS REPORTED TO THEM BY A NEIGHBOR. THE CALLER TO 911 STATED THEY HAD WITNESSED AN ALLEGED EXPLOSION WHEN THE HOME CAUGHT FIRE. A UTILITY FIELD TECHNICIAN ARRIVED AT THE RESIDENCE AT APPROXIMATELY 10:36 AM ON 3/1/2021 AND SHUT OFF THE GAS FLOW TO THE HOME. A LEAK SURVEY TECHNICIAN ARRIVED AT APPROXIMATELY 1:39 PM AND TESTED THE SOIL FOR POSSIBLE GAS LEAKS ALONG THE COMPANY SERVICE LINE.  BAR HOLE TESTS WERE MADE WITH A GAS MEASUREMENT INDICATOR AND A RMLD. GAS WAS DETECTED AT POINTS ALONG THE OPERATOR'S SERVICE LINE TO THE METER, AS WELL AS MIGRATION TOWARD THE HOME, PERCENTAGES WERE IN PPM. THE OPERATOR'S STEEL GAS SERVICE LINE LEADING FROM THE MAIN TO THE INLET SIDE OF THE METER WAS UNCOVERED BY EXCAVATION, TECHNICIANS DISCOVERED CORROSION AND A 1/16" PIT THROUGH THE PIPE WALL 21 FT. NORTH OF THE METER. THIS PITTING WAS DETERMINED TO BE THE CAUSE OF THE GAS DETECTED BY THE BAR HOLE TESTING. THE CUSTOMER SERVICE LINE WAS A DISTANCE OF 19FT 10.5" FROM THE OUTLET SIDE OF THE METER TO THE HOME, THE LINE WAS PRESSURED TESTED BY A SEPARATE PARTY AND THE RESULTS DID NOT INDICATE A LEAK. 1720.NARRATIVE: THE EXCAVATOR WAS WORKING ON THE ACCESS ROAD FOR THE ENTRANCE TO THE NEW SHOPPING CENTER. THE PROJECT HAS BEEN ONGOING SINCE FEBRUARY. THEY HAD NOT STARTED ON THIS SECTION UNTIL THE LAST COUPLE OF MONTHS. AFTER REMOVING AN OLD DRIVEWAY THAT EXISTED ALONG THE ROAD THEY HAD CHANGED THE GRADE OF THE AREA BY REMOVING A PORTION OF THE DIRT THAT COVERED THE 6" MAIN. THERE HAD BEEN A LOCATE DONE FOR A FIBER CONTRACTOR THAT WAS BASICALLY ALONG THE SAME PATH OF THE ROAD CONTRACTORS WORKSITE. THE MAIN WAS FLAGGED AND MARKED CORRECTLY ALONG THE PATH. ALL THE MARKINGS WERE PRESENT WHEN BURTS CONSTRUCTION REMOVED SOME MORE MATERIAL WITH A DOZER AND THEN BROUGHT IN A RECLAIMER TO MIX THE DIRT AND ROAD BASE FOR STABILIZATION. WHEN THE MIXER STARTED TO TILL THE DIRT IT HIT THE LINE DAMAGING IT AND CAUSING AN IGNITION. THE EQUIPMENT OPERATOR SHUT OFF THE MACHINE AND JUMPED OFF BUT BUT DID GET HIS RIGHT ARM BURNT TO THE POINT HE WAS TAKEN TO THE HOSPITAL BY HELICOPTER. THE RECLAIMER WAS ENGULFED IN FLAMES AND COMPLETELY DESTROYED. WE CLOSED A VALVE OFF ON THE WEST SIDE OF THE DAMAGE AND THEN DUG UP THE 6" AND SQUEEZED IT OFF TO STOP THE FLOW OF GAS ON THE EAST SIDE. THE FIRE DEPARTMENT PUT THE FIRE OUT. I CONTACTED THE RRC BY PHONE AND ALSO THE NRC. THE RRC SENT INVESTIGATORS OUT TO ACCESS THE SCENE AND INVESTIGATE IT. I CHECKED ON THE EMPLOYEE WHO WAS INJURED AND HIS SUPERVISOR SAID HE WAS RELEASED FROM THE HOSPITAL THAT SAME NIGHT WITH SEVERE BURNS ON HIS RIGHT ARM.  THE DAMAGED RECLAIMER WAS REMOVED FROM THE SPOT ON THE 25TH OF OCTOBER 2021. ON TUESDAY THE 26TH OCTOBER 2021 WE DUG UP, LOWERED AND REPAIRED THE LINE WAS DAMAGED WITH THE RRC INSPECTORS ON SITE. ON THURSDAY THE GAS DEPARTMENT EXPOSED THE GAS MAIN ALONG THE AREA IN 4 DIFFERENT SPOTS VERIFYING ITS LOCATION AND DEPTH. ALL WERE ALREADY CORRECTLY MARKED BUT THESE AREAS HAD NOT HAD DIRT REMOVED FROM THE TOP OF THEM.    THE CITY OF BRENHAM GAS DEPOARTMENT WILL CONTINUE TO MARK OUR FACILITIES IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE TEXAS AMINISTRATIVE CODE TITLE 16 PART 1 CHAPTER 18 FOR UNDERGROUND PIPELINE DAMAGE PREVENTION. WE HAVE PUT IN PLACE IN OUR PLAN REVIEW FOR DEVELOPEMENT SERVICES UNDER THE GAS DEPARTMENT COMMENTS SECTION VERBIAGE STATING THAT THE BUILDER, CONTRACTOR, DEVELOPER AND/OR EXCAVATORS THAT TAKE PART IN THESE WORK PROJECTS WILL MAINTAIN CONTACT WITH THE CITY OF BRENHAM AND BE AWARE OF THEIR RESPONSIBILITY OF PROTECTION OF EXISTING CITY UNTILITIES ON THESE SITES DURING THE DURATION OF THE PROJECT.

22364.NARRATIVE: GAS CREW WAS INSTALLING A NEW 3/4 INCH PE SERVICE LINE WITH A PLASTIC BOLT ON SERVICE TEE ON A 4" PE MAIN. THE SERVICE LINE BEING INSTALLED WITH AN EFV WAS CONNECTED TO THE SERVICE TEE AT THE MAIN. THE TAP CUTTER ON THE SERVICE TEE WAS SCREWED CLOCKWISE TO TAP INTO THE MAIN TO PROVIDE GAS TO THE NEW CUSTOMER. AFTER TAP WAS COMPLETED AND THE GAS HAD BEEN INTRODUCED INTO THE SERVICE LINE FOR APPROXIMATELY 30 MINUTES, THE TAP SIDE OF THE EFV, THE FITTING (NUT THAT FASTENS THE EFV TO THE TAP) BLEW OFF. THE EMPLOYEE THAT WAS INJURED JUMPED INTO THE HOLE AND ATTEMPTED TO SCREW THE TAP CUTTER BACK DOWN INTO THE MAIN TO STOP GAS FLOW. WHILE TURNING THE TAP, APPROXIMATELY 2 ROUNDS, THE GAS IGNITED.  THE INDIVIDUAL JUMPED OUT OF THE HOLE AND A CREW MEMBER WENT TO A CLOSE BY MAIN LINE VALVE TO TURN OFF THE GAS FEEDING THE DAMAGED SERVICE LINE. THIS MAIN LINE VALVE SHUT OFF GAS DOWNSTREAM OF THE CLOSED VALVE. THERE WAS A WATER SERVICE LOCATED IN THE SAME EXCAVATION THAT MELTED AND THE WATER EXTINGUISHED THE FIRE. THE MAIN LINE VALVE WAS TURNED OFF ELIMINATING THE GAS FLOW.

2392.NARRATIVE: THE FINDINGS OF THE INVESTIGATION BY THE FIRE DEPARTMENT REVEALED THE HOMEOWNER HAD INSTALLED A FIRE PIT DIRECTLY OVER THE NATURAL GAS DISTRIBUTION SERVICE LINE.  THE NATURAL GAS SERVICE LINE IS A 1/2" PLASTIC DISTRIBUTION SERVICE LINE INSERTED INSIDE AN ABANDON 1 1/4" STEEL LINE.  THE HEAT FROM THE FIRE, WITHIN THE FIREPIT, HEATED THE 1 1/4" STEEL CASING LINE THEREFORE CREATING A HOLE IN THE 1/2" PLASTIC SERVICE LINE THAT WAS INSERTED WITHIN THE 1 1/4" STEEL CASING LINE.  THIS HOLE ALLOWED GAS TO ESCAPE INSIDE THE CASING AND TRAVEL TO THE RESIDENTIAL HOME IT WAS SERVING, 558 N. RYBOLT AVE.  ACCUMULATION OF THE NATURAL GAS OCCURRED WITHIN THE HOME AND WAS IGNITED BY THE CUSTOMER WHEN HE TRIED TO LIGHT A CIGARETTE.  CEG'S OWN INVESTIGATION FINDINGS WERE CONSISTENT WITH THE FIRE DEPARTMENT'S.

39257.NARRATIVE: THE INTERIOR GAS UTILITY (IGU) LNG STORAGE AND VAPORIZATION SITE NUMBER 3 (SS3) IN FAIRBANKS, ALASKA SENT COLD GAS AND POSSIBLY LNG TO THE DISTRIBUTION SYSTEM.  WHEN THE COLD GAS OR LNG ENTERED THE DISTRIBUTION SYSTEM, IT EMBRITTLED THE 8' UNDERGROUND HDPE PIPE, WHICH SUBSEQUENTLY RUPTURED IN A SECTION OF PIPING WITHIN IGU PROPERTY.  THE HIGHEST RECORDED PRESSURE DOWNSTREAM OF THE DISTRIBUTION REGULATORS AT SS3 WAS 62PSIG.  AT APPROXIMATELY 4:10PM ON 11/21/2021, A TEMPERATURE SWITCH ON THE OUTLET OF THE VAPORIZER MALFUNCTIONED AND CLOSED A VALVE TO STOP THE FLOW OF LNG THROUGH THE VAPORIZER.  WITH NO LNG TO VAPORIZE, THE GLYCOL HEATER TURNED OFF DUE TO LOW DEMAND.  AT ABOUT 4:55PM, AN OPERATOR NOTICED THAT THE FLOW OF LNG HAD STOPPED, AND THE DISTRIBUTION PRESSURE WAS DROPPING.  THE OPERATOR OPENED THE CLOSED VAPORIZER VALVE VIA REMOTE CONTROL.  THE OPERATOR DID NOT NOTICE THAT THE BOILER WAS NOT FIRING AND DID NOT MONITOR THE SITE LONG ENOUGH TO VERIFY THE SYSTEM WAS STABLE AND PROPER TEMPERATURES WHERE BEING MAINTAINED.  DUE TO THE MALFUNCTIONING TEMPERATURE SWITCH AND A TEMPERATURE TRANSMITTER THAT HAD NOT BEEN PROGRAMMED TO ACT AS A BACKUP TO THE TEMPERATURE SWITCH, THE CONTROL SYSTEM DID NOT STOP THE FLOW OF LNG THROUGH THE VAPORIZER, UPON A LOW GAS TEMPERATURE ON THE OUTLET OF THE VAPORIZER.  THE BOILER ATTEMPTED TO FIRE ABOUT THREE MINUTES AFTER THE LNG FLOW RESUMED BUT FAILED TO STAY RUNNING.  THE SYSTEM ATTEMPTED TO START A BACK-UP BOILER ABOUT 10 MINUTES LATER, ABOUT WHEN THE DISTRIBUTION LINE RUPTURED.  THE STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURES WILL BE REVISED TO NO LONGER ALLOW CONTROL CHANGES FROM VIA REMOTE CONTROL (EXCEPT FOR EMERGENCY SHUT DOWNS AND SPECIFIED EXCEPTIONS) AND INSTEAD REQUIRE THE MONITORING OPERATOR TO TRAVEL TO THE SITE TO MAKE THE NECESSARY ADJUSTMENTS AND CHANGES.  THE VAPORIZER TEMPERATURE SWITCHES WILL BE RECOMMISSIONED, AND THE TEMPERATURE TRANSMITTERS WILL BE ADDED INTO THE VAPORIZER SHUTDOWN PROGRAMMING LOGIC TO ADD REDUNDANCY.  ADDITIONALLY, A DOWNSTREAM TEMPERATURE TRANSMITTER LOCATED ON THE METER SKID WILL BE USED TO SHUT DOWN THE LNG PUMPS IF LOW TEMPERATURE IS DETECTED INDICATING THE VAPORIZER SHUTDOWNS FAILED TO ACTIVATE AS A RESULT OF LOW OUTLET TEMPERATURE.

2456.NARRATIVE: REPORTABLE INCIDENT NARRATIVE    ON 1 DECEMBER 2021, AT APPROXIMATELY 11:23 HOURS, A CMC GAS CREW COMMISSIONING A NEW 2-INCH MDPE MAIN OF APPROXIMATELY 6,100 LF EXPERIENCED AN UNEXPECTED INCIDENT WHERE THE VENTING GAS IGNITED, INJURING ONE EMPLOYEE.  INJURIES CONSISTED OF NON-LIFE-THREATENING BURNS ON HIS UPPER BODY.    A 2.0 X 0.75-INCH, HIGH-VOLUME TAP WAS INSTALLED ON THE OUTLET END OF THE PIPELINE SEGMENT.  NATURAL GAS WAS INTRODUCED INTO THE PIPELINE SEGMENT FROM THE SUPPLY END OF THE PIPELINE FROM A "FARM TAP" REGULATOR STATION.  GAS FLOWED, PUSHING THE AIR OUT OF THE PIPELINE FOR APPROXIMATELY 8 MINUTES.    AT APPROXIMATELY THE 8-MINUTE MARK OF THE PURGE, THE PURGE TECHNICIAN (TECH 1) ON THE SITE APPROACHED THE TAP TEE WHERE GAS WAS VENTING.  AS TECH 1 REACHED FOR THE TAP, AN UNEXPECTED IGNITION OF THE GAS OCCURRED.    BEFORE BEING ABLE TO REMOVE HIMSELF FROM THE FLASH, TECH 1 RECEIVED MINOR BURNS ON THE FACE AND ARM AREAS.  THE FIRE-WATCH TECHNICIAN (TECH 3) NOTIFIED THE TECHNICIAN OPERATING THE SUPPLY VALVE (TECH 2) OF THE INCIDENT AND REQUESTED THE SUPPLY VALVE BE CLOSED.  AS THE VOLUME OF GAS IN THE PIPE DIMINISHED, THE TECH 3 EXTINGUISHED THE SMALL FLAME. APPROXIMATE 5 MINUTES ELAPSED FROM THE TIME OF IGNITION UNTIL THE FLAME WAS EXTINGUISHED.    ON-SITE PERSONNEL NOTIFIED THE CONSTRUCTION AND MAINTENANCE MANAGER, WHO NOTIFIED OTHER MANAGEMENT.  ON SITE PERSONNEL TRANSPORTED THE INJURED TECHNICIAN TO THE LOCAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY ROOM, APPROXIMATELY 3 MILES AWAY.  TECH 1 WAS TREATED AND TRANSPORTED TO UNIVERSITY HOSPITAL IN MOBILE, ALABAMA, WHERE HE WAS ADMITTED FOR FURTHER TREATMENT AND OBSERVATION.    CMC GAS PERSONNEL PLACED A PIPE SQUEEZE DEVICE ON THE 2-INCH MDPE PIPE UNTIL THE PIPE WAS CUT AND CAPPED.    UPON NOTIFICATION OF THE HOSPITALIZATION OF TECH 1 AT 17:24 HOURS, THE COMPLIANCE MANAGER NOTIFIED THE ALABAMA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION, PIPELINE SAFETY DIVISION OF THE INCIDENT, AND THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER.  THIS CALL WAS MADE AT 17:43 HOURS.    TECH 1 WAS RELEASED FROM THE UNIVERSITY HOSPITAL ON DECEMBER 8TH AND WAS SUBSEQUENTLY RELEASED TO RETURN TO WORK ON 20 DECEMBER 2021.    AT THE TIME OF THIS REPORT, THE INVESTIGATION HAS REVEALED THE FOLLOWING:    1) THE BELIEVED SOURCE OF IGNITION WAS STATIC ELECTRICITY.           A. AT THE TIME OF THE IGNITION, THE AMBIENT AIR RELATIVE HUMIDITY WAS REPORTED AT 20%           B. AT THE TIME OF THE IGNITION, THE AMBIENT AIR TEMPERATURE WAS REPORTED AT 72 DEGREES FAHRENHEIT.    2) THE UTILIZED GROUNDING TECHNIQUES (TO MITIGATE STATIC ELECTRICITY) WERE INCONSISTENT WITH CMC GAS POLICY.    3) INCONSISTENT WITH CMC GAS POLICY, TECH 1 FAILED TO EMPLOY A VENT STACK ON THE VENT OUTLET TO DIRECT THE GAS FLOW UPWARD.    4) TECH 2 (THE VALVE OPERATOR ON THE SUPPLY END OF THE PIPELINE) WAS DETERMINED TO BE WORKING OUTSIDE HIS OPERATOR QUALIFICATION.    5) TECH 1, WHO WAS ALSO MONITORING THE PURGE OF GAS DID NOT EMPLOY A COMBUSTIBLE GAS METER (CGI) OR A PERSONAL PROTECTIVE ATMOSPHERIC METER, INCONSISTENT WITH CMC GAS POLICY.    6) TECH 1 DID NOT DON THE FIRE-RESISTANT CLOTHING AND OTHER PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT (PPE) WHICH WERE PROVIDED BY CMC GAS AND IS CMC GAS STANDARD PROCEDURE.      MITIGATIVE MEASURES TAKEN TO PREVENT RECURRENCE:    1)     ALL RELEVANT MEMBERS OF THE 12/01/21 INCIDENT CREW HAVE BEEN DISQUALIFIED, RETRAINED, AND REQUALIFIED ON RELEVANT OQ TASKS.    2)     ALL RELEVANT MEMBERS OF THE 12/01/21 INCIDENT CREW HAVE ATTENDED A POLICY, STATIC MITIGATION, AND PPE REVIEW SESSION.    3)     INTERNAL DISCIPLINARY ACTIONS TAKEN AS RELEVANT.

THE BORE WAS FOR THE INSTALLATION OF A 42 INCH WATER MAIN WITHIN A 54" CASING. THE GAS MAIN WAS PROPERLY LOCATED AND THE CONTRACTOR FAILED TO PERFORM DUE DILIGENCE IN ACCORDANCE WITH NORTH CAROLINA GENERAL STATUTES CHAPTER 87 ARTICLE 8A - UNDERGROUND UTILITY SAFETY AND DAMAGE PREVENTION ACT.  THE GAS MAIN WAS RUPTURED BY THE AUGER BORE MACHINE CAUSING THE RELEASE OF NATURAL GAS AND REQUIRING THE REPAIR OF THE GAS LINE. REPAIRS TO THE CITY OF MONROE NATURAL GAS MAIN WERE FINALIZED ON 01/06/2022 AT 3:30 AM.     ON 1/04/2022 AT 05:15 PM THE CITY OF MONROE DETERMINED THAT THE INCIDENT REPORTING THRESHOLD WAS GOING TO BE MET BEFORE THE FACILITIES COULD BE REPAIRED. THEREFORE A DETERMINATION OF FILING THE INITIAL INCIDENT WITH NRC WAS MADE. THE NRC NOTIFICATION WAS MADE AT APPROXIMATELY 6:00 PM ON 1/4/2022. THE ACTUAL INCIDENT THRESHOLD OF 3,000 MCF WAS NOT MET UNTIL APPROXIMATELY 1/05/2022 AT APPROXIMATELY 05:26 AM.    CDM WAS NEGLIGENT IN THE FOLLOWING REQUIREMENTS: NC ARTICLE 8A - UNDERGROUND UTILITY SAFETY AND DAMAGE PREVENTION ACT - 87-122. EXCAVATOR RESPONSIBILITIES    C) AN EXCAVATOR SHALL COMPLY WITH THE FOLLOWING:  (3) PLAN THE EXCAVATION OR DEMOLITION TO AVOID DAMAGE TO OR MINIMIZE INTERFERENCE WITH FACILITIES IN OR NEAR THE CONSTRUCTION AREA. 18508.NARRATIVE: DCI WAS CONTRACTED BY CENTERPOINT INDIANA-ELECTRIC TO INSTALL UNDERGROUND ELECTRIC LINES AND A NEW JUNCTION BOX IN THE GREEN SPACE ACROSS FROM 2710 WINDEMERE DRIVE, EVANSVILLE, INDIANA 47725 (VANDERBURGH COUNTY). DCI HAD SUBCONTRACTED THE EXCAVATION WORK OUT TO EARLEY ELECTRIC.  ON MAY 23, 2022, LESTER KNEPP WITH EARLEY ELECTRIC WAS OPERATING A CATERPILLAR 304E MINI EXCAVATOR TO EXPOSE UNDERGROUND ELECTRIC LINES ALONG THE SOUTH SIDE OF WINDEMERE DRIVE. DCI HAD CALLED FOR LOCATES BY CALLING INDIANA 811 AND GOT A LOCATE TICKET # 2205092040 ON MAY 9, 2022. EARLEY ELECTRIC AND MR. KNEPP WERE UNDER THE MISTAKEN IMPRESSION THEY COULD EXCAVATE UNDER DCI'S LOCATE AND THEREFORE DID NOT CALL FOR THEIR OWN LOCATE TICKET.  AT APPROXIMATELY 1530HR., MR. KNEPP, WHILE OPERATING THE MINI EXCAVATOR, HIT A 2' PE UNDERGROUND GAS MAIN OWNED AND OPERATED BY SOUTHERN INDIANA GAS AND ELECTRIC COMPANY D.B.A CENTERPOINT ENERGY INDIANA ' SOUTH. THE GAS MAIN WAS OPERATING AT APPROXIMATELY 58 PSIG. EARLEY ELECTRIC EMPLOYEE AARON SCHROER WITNESSED THE EVENT, STATING MR. KNEPP UPON HITTING THE MAIN, EXITED THE EXCAVATOR LEAVING IT RUNNING. ACCORDING TO MR. SCHROER, THE GAS WAS BLOWING FOR ABOUT 25 SECONDS BEFORE IT IGNITED. MR. SCHROER NOTIFIED 911 IMMEDIATELY AT APPROXIMATELY 1530HRS. MR. SCHROER STATED THEY DID NOT NOTICE THE GAS LOCATE MARKS THAT WERE PART OF DCI'S MAY 9TH LOCATE TICKET. THE LOCATE WAS PERFORMED ON MAY 10, 2022. LOCATE PICTURES FROM THAT DATE SHOW THE GAS FACILITY WERE PROPERLY FLAGGED AND MARKED. AT THE TIME OF THE EVENT, GAS FACILITY LOCATE FLAGS HAD BEEN REMOVED AND MARKS WERE FAINT. CENTERPOINT DISPATCH WAS NOTIFIED BY 911 DISPATCH APPROXIMATELY 1535HRS. CENTERPOINT GAS CREW WAS NOTIFIED AT 1543HRS. AND ARRIVED ON SCENE AT 1615HRS. THE GAS FROM THE MAIN WAS STILL BURNING. THE PE MAIN WAS DUEL FED SO THE CENTERPOINT GAS CREW DUG UP AND EXPOSED THE MAIN ON THE EAST AND WEST SIDE OF THE DAMAGE. THE GAS CREW PERFORMED SQUEEZE OFF OPERATIONS STOPPING THE FLOW OF GAS AND EXTINGUISHING THE FIRE AT 1700HRS. PRIOR TO SQUEEZING OFF, TWO CUSTOMERS WERE TAKEN OUT OF SERVICE SO THAT GAUGES COULD BE INSTALLED. AT THE TIME OF INSTALLATION, THE EAST GAUGE READ 25PSIG WHERE THE WEST SIDE READ 4PSIG. AFTER SQUEEZE OFF, PRESSURE ON BOTH SIDES RETURN TO NEAR NORMAL PRESSURES.   CENTERPOINT DISPATCH SENT OUT AN EMAIL ALERTING STAKEHOLDER, INCLUDING MEMBERS OF THE INDIANA UTILITY REGULATORY COMMISSION, PIPELINE SAFETY DEPARTMENT OF THE INITIAL REPORT FROM 911 AT 1545HRS. CENTERPOINT PIPELINE SAFETY AND COMPLIANCE DEPARTMENT WAS IN CONTACT WITH MEMBERS OF THE INDIANA UTILITY REGULATORY COMMISSION, PIPELINE SAFETY DEPARTMENT SHORTLY THEREAFTER. INDIANA UTILITY REGULATORY COMMISSION, PIPELINE SAFETY DEPARTMENT, CHIEF ENGINEER RICH MEDCALF ARRIVED ON SCENE AND INVESTIGATED. LOCAL NEWS MEDIA COVERAGE AS WELL AS MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC POSTED VIDEO OF THE FIRE ON SOCIAL MEDIA SITES. ON BOTH SIDES OF THE DAMAGE, THE MAIN WAS CUT AND CAPPED OFF A SHORT DISTANCE FROM WHERE IT WAS SQUEEZED OFF. IT HAS YET TO BE DETERMINED IF OR WHEN THE MAIN WILL BE RESTORED TO DUAL FED STATUS.  CENTERPOINT PIPELINE SAFETY AND COMPLIANCE DEPARTMENT LEAD OPERATION SPECIALIST DECIDED TO CONTACT THE NRC, DESPITE THE EVENT NOT MEETING REPORT CRITERIA, DUE TO THE AMOUNT OF ATTENTION AND VIDEO.

18704.NARRATIVE: ON NOVEMBER 10TH 2022, I (FOREMAN) AND THE REST OF MY CREW WERE INSTALLING A SECTION OF NEW GAS MAIN INSIDE THE CITY LIMITS OF SULLIVAN IL. UPON SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THE DRILLING PROCESS TECHNICIAN 1 RAISED THE SHELL CUTTER INTO THE DRILLING MACHINE CHAMBER AND THE GATE VALVE WAS CLOSED TO STOP OFF GAS FLOW FROM THE TOP OF THE TEE. THE DRILLING MACHINE WAS DISASSEMBLED FROM THE GATE VALVE AND THE SHELL CUTTER DISASSEMBLED AND THE COMPLETION PLUG INSTALLED. ONCE TECHNICIAN 1 REASSEMBLED THE MACHINE IT WAS REATTACHED TO THE TOP OF THE GATE VALVE AND THE VALVE WAS OPENED ALLOWING THE COMPLETION PLUG TO BE LOWERED INTO THE TOP OF THE TEE AND THREADED INTO IT. ONCE THE PLUG WAS THREADED INTO THE TEE AND TIGHT THE SHAFT WAS REMOVED FROM THE COMPLETION PLUG AND THE MACHINE WAS REMOVED AGAIN FROM THE GATE VALVE. THE GATE VALVE WAS THEN REMOVED AND THE COMPLETION PLUG WRENCH WAS PUT INTO THE TOP OF THE COMPLETION PLUG BY TECHNICIAN 1. TECHNICIAN 1 PERFORMED ALL THE ASSEMBLY AND DISASSEMBLY OF THE MACHINE. TECHNICIAN 1 THEN TURNED THE PLUG TIGHTENING IT INTO THE TEE A 1/4 - 1/2 TURN AND THEN HANDED THE WRENCH TO TECHNICIAN 3 AND TOLD HIM TO FINISH TIGHTENING THE PLUG. TECHNICIAN 3 THEN FITTED THE WRENCH INTO THE TOP OF THE COMPLETION PLUG. HE IS RIGHT HANDED SO HE PUT HIS LEFT HAND ON TOP OF THE WRENCH TO SECURE IT AND HIS RIGHT HAND ON THE HANDLE TO TURN IT. AS SOON AS HE STARTED TO TURN THE PLUG IT BLEW OUT THE TOP. AT THE TIME THAT IT BLEW OUT I (FOREMAN) WAS SEATED ON THE EAST EDGE OF THE BELL HOLE, TECHNICIAN 2 WAS SEATED ON THE SOUTH EDGE, TECHNICIAN 3 WAS STANDING IN THE SOUTH WEST CORNER OF THE PREEXISTING AND NEW MAINS AND TECHNICIAN 1 WAS STANDING IN THE NORTH WEST CORNER OF THE PREEXISTING AND NEW MAINS. I ROLLED AWAY FROM THE EXCAVATION. I LOOKED TO MY LEFT AND SAW THAT TECHNICIAN 2 WAS CLEAR OF THE HOLE. I LOOKED RIGHT AND SAW TECHNICIAN 3 MOVING WEST IN THE DITCH AWAY FROM IT. I LOOKED RIGHT AND SAW TECHNICIAN 1 LOOKING AROUND ALL AROUND HIM I YELLED ARE YOU OK AND HE GAVE ME A THUMBS UP AND CONTINUED LOOKING AROUND HIM. I LOOKED AT TECHNICIAN 3 AND SAW HIS FACE WAS OBVIOUS SHOCK. I SAW HIM HOLDING HIS LEFT ARM AND THEN SAW HIS ARM STARTING TO BLEED. I THEN RAN AROUND THE NORTH SIDE OF THE HOLE AND GRABBED TECHNICIAN 3 AND PULLED HIM OUT OF THE DITCH AND TOOK HIM TO GET A FIRST AID KIT. AT THIS TIME I SAW HOW BAD HIS ARM WAS BLEEDING SO I KEYED UP ON THE CITY RADIO AND STATED SULLIVAN EMS SULLIVAN EMS YOU ARE NEEDED NOW AT THE H&R BLOCK BUILDING ON SOUTH HAMILTON STREET INJURED CITY EMPLOYEE WITH SHRAPNEL WOUNDS TO HIS LEFT FOREARM AND BICEP WITH SEVERE BLEEDING. I REPEATED THIS MESSAGE TWICE ON THE RADIO. I THEN TURNED TO TECHNICIAN 3 AND BEGAN MEDICAL TRIAGE. HE SAID IT FEELS LIKE SOMETHING IS MOVING UP MY ARM! I THEN TOOK OFF MY LEATHER BELT AND TOLD HIM IM GONNA TIE OFF YOUR ARM! I USED MY BELT JUST BELOW HIS LEFT ARMPIT TO APPLY A TOURNIQUET. I WRAPPED IT TIGHT AND GAVE HIM THE LOOSE END AND TOLD HIM TO HOLD IT AND NOT LET GO UNTIL THE EMTS TOLD HIM TO. MOMENTS LATER EMTS ARRIVED AND TOOK TECHNICIAN 3 TO ST MARYS HOSPITAL BY AMBULANCE IN DECATUR IL. I TURNED BACK TO TECHNICIANS 1 AND 2 AND THEY HAD ALREADY PUT THE GATE VALVE BACK ON AND SHUT DOWN THE GAS. TECHNICIAN 1 AND I PUT A NEW COMPLETION PLUG IN THE TEE AND THEN SECURED THE AREA AND WENT TO DO DRUG SCREENINGS PER HUMAN RESOURCES.

NO LEAKS WERE DETECTED ON THE SERVICE OR ON THE MAIN IN THE VICINITY OF THE PROPERTY. THE COMPANY HAS NOT BEEN INFORMED BY DPU, FIRE DEPARTMENT, OR THE STATE FIRE MARSHAL OF THEIR FINDINGS OF THE CAUSE OF THE EVENT.     PART A.11. IT IS UNDETERMINED WHETHER A FAILURE OCCURRED, THE COMPANY WAS INFORMED OF THE EVENT BY THE TAUNTON, MA POLICE DEPARTMENT.  PART A.21. NO LEAKS WERE DETECTED ON THE SERVICE OR ON THE MAIN IN THE VICINITY OF THE PROPERTY  PART A.22. THE COMPANY CANNOT CONFIRM THE NUMBER OF GENERAL PUBLIC EVACUATED.    PART D.2.A THE PUBLIC AND NON-OPERATOR PRIVATE PROPERTY DAMAGE IS BASED ON THE TAUNTON ASSESSOR DATABASE FOR 2026 ASSESSMENTS.  PART D.2.C. ESTIMATED COST IS UNKNOWN AT THIS TIME.    PART E.6 THE POINT OF FAILURE IS UNKNOWN AND NO DETECTABLE LEAKS WERE NOTED ON THE SERVICE OR MAIN IN THE VICINITY OF THE PROPERTY.

15845.NARRATIVE: ON 3/21/26 AT 12:34, PIE&G ON CALL SUPERVISOR RECEIVED A CALL FROM OUR AFTER HOURS DISPATCH TO RESPOND TO A STRUCTURE FIRE ON CAULKINS LK RD. OUR SOUTH GAS STANDBY TECHNICIAN WAS IN THE FIELD WORKING ON OTHER CALLS, SO SUPERVISOR CALLED THE NEXT AVAILABLE TECH TO RESPOND. TECH ARRIVED ON SCENE AT 14:03 AND FOUND HOUSE FULLY INVOLVED IN THE FIRE AND MOSTLY CONSUMED. TECH NOTED GAS BURNING IN THE AREA OF THE RISER. FIRE AT RISER WENT OUT, LEAVING GAS BLOWING INTO THE REMAINS OF THE BURNING HOUSE. TECH WAS NOT ABLE TO APPROACH HOUSE DUE TO CONCERN OF SECONDARY IGNITION OF GAS. TECH RESPONDED BY LOCATING SERVICE LINE AND CAPPING THE LINE NEAR THE ROAD, ELIMINATING GAS FLOW TO THE RISER AT THE HOUSE. DUE TO SMOKE AND CONGESTION OF EMERGENCY RESPONDERS AT THE SCENE, THE TECH COMPLETE THE PAPERWORK FOR STRUCTURE FIRE RESPONSE AND LEFT THE SCENE WITH NO FURTHER INVESTIGATION.     ON 3/25/26 AND EMAIL WAS SENT TO THE DIRECTOR OF GAS OPERATIONS BY MPSC STAFF INQUIRING ABOUT AN EXPLOSION ON PIE&G SYSTEM THAT WAS NOT REPORTED. DIRECTOR RESPONDED THAT WE HAD RESPONDED TO A STRUCTURE FIRE BUT HAD NO KNOWLEDGE OF AN EXPLOSION. MPSC REITERATED THAT THERE HAD BEEN AN EXPLOSION ACCORDING TO FIRE DEPT. PIE&G CONTACTED THE RESPONDING TECH AND ASKED IF THERE WAS A POSSIBILITY THAT THE HOUSE EXPLODED. TECH RESPONDED THERE WAS NOT, AS THE WALLS TO THE HOME HAD COLLAPSED INTO THE HOME, NOT OUT OF THE HOME AS WOULD BE NORMAL IN AN EXPLOSION. TECH WAS DISPATCHED TO GO BACK TO THE SCENE AND INVESTIGATE FURTHER. TECH NOTED THERE WAS MORE DEBRIS IN THE YARD THAN HAD BEEN VISIBLE DURING THE INITIAL RESPONSE DUE TO THE CONGESTION FROM THE RESPONDERS AND THE SMOKE AT THE SCENE. INSURANCE INVESTIGATOR WAS ON SCENE AND WAS RULING THE INCIDENT AN EXPLOSION. TECH INTERVIEWED NEIGHBORS WHO STATED THAT THERE WAS A MUFFLED NOISE AND WHEN THEY LOOKED OUT, THERE WAS SOME INSULATION/DEBRIS AIRBORNE IN THE YARD. TECH DISCOVERED THE RISER WAS SNAPPED OFF BELOW THE METER VALVE, AND THAT THERE WAS REMAINING CHUNKS OF ICE ON THE GROUND IN THE AREA OF THE RISER. AN ADDITIONAL CREW WAS DISPATCHED TO THE SCENE TO CONDUCT A PRESSURE TEST OF THE SERVICE LINE FROM THE POINT IT HAD BEEN CAPPED TO THE RISER. AIR TESTED AT 137# FOR 14 MINUTES, TEST PASSED. INFORMATION WAS BROUGHT BACK TO PIE&G HEADQUARTERS FOR REVIEW.     ON 3/26/26 GAS PERSONNEL MET TO REVIEW ADDITIONAL INFORMATION REGARDING THE INCIDENT. MPSC STAFF CONTACTED PIE&G TO QUESTION WHY NO REPORT HAD BEEN FILED. AFTER ADDITIONAL INFORMATION HAD BEEN REVIEWED, PIE&G DID DETERMINE THAT THERE HAD BEEN AN EXPLOSION, AND MADE TELEPHONIC REPORTS TO THE MPSC & NRC ACCORDINGLY.     ON 3/30/26 MPSC AGAIN CONTACTED PIE&G AND STATED THAT WE HAD NOT FILED A 48 HOUR UPDATE TO THE REPORT. PIE&G CONDUCTED AN INTERNET SEARCH OF 191.5 WHICH DID NOT INCLUDE THE 48 HOUR PROVISION, NOR WAS THAT INFORMATION RELAYED TO PIE&G DURING THE INITIAL REPORT. PIE&G CALLED IN A 48 HOUR UPDATE TO THE NRC LINE WITH NO FURTHER INFORMATION.     3/25/26-4/17/26 PIE&G PERSONNEL GATHERED ALL INFORMATION RELATED TO THE INCIDENT TO FINALIZE THE INVESTIGATION AND COMPLETE THE FINAL REPORT.
